data.body:
Operator decision (2026-08-19): APPROVED decomposition. Re-typed task -> epic and split into three
child stories, ordered by CONTRACT BOUNDARIES FIRST (not by defect count), per the description's own
Approach section.

Children:
  1. wellborn-earnest-hermitcrab (2cdd-e9d3-e42b-4709) — rebar.llm.*        (293 untyped, ~165 Any)
  2. glassy-handsewn-banteng     (201d-64e2-537c-4df6) — rebar._commands.*  (146 untyped)
  3. creative-overcooked-perch   (5f7f-528f-031e-4919) — rebar._engine.*    (134 untyped, ~224 Any)

llm goes first because it carries the provider/prompt/output contracts the other two consume;
_commands depends_on llm (recorded as a blocking link).

PREREQUISITE FILED SEPARATELY, per the operator's instruction: ffbb-9c27-78ac-489b — "Split
llm/plan_review/pass1.py (at the 800 LOC cap) along an existing call-graph seam". That file is AT the
cap, so annotating it fails the module-size gate; the split must land before the llm child. Note the
mechanics: because the split ticket is standalone (not a child of this epic), the depends_on link
ESCALATED to the nearest common ancestor and is recorded at THIS epic's level rather than on the llm
child. Effect is equivalent and slightly stronger — nothing under this epic should start until the
split lands — but read the link there, not on the child.

CORRECTION to the epic's stated collision: the description warns that this work "collides with the
reconciler port-boundary work already scoped by cc77-8120-bcc6-47e8". That ticket is now CLOSED, as
is its parent e369-a449-4773-48fb, so the collision no longer blocks the _engine child and no
blocking link was recorded for it. The live consequence is different: those seams have MOVED, so the
residue counts above (measured on main @ ea6ee67e6a) are stale and must be re-measured at claim time.

Tier 2 (disallow_any_explicit) remains a separate later step for all three packages; each child
promotes to tier 1 only.
